The Master Plan for General Mitchell Field has projections of 6,000 autmobile parking spaces needed by 1990 to accommodate the public as compared to 1,500 existing now. Fifty percent of all public automobiles which parked at the airport entered the short-term parking lot nearest the airport terminal building. Service employees could be shuttled by bus if the need arises but service to the airport clientel would not lend to shuttle bus operations.
Present FHWA design criteria regulations for the Airport

Spur specifically do not allow ramping off to parking lots along\nits length except at the terminal ends. On site surveys by SEURPC\nindicate that 70 to 80% of those desiring air carrier service use
Mitchell Field with 25% traveling to O'Hare Field in Chicago since
there are more flights to more areas. Providing easier access
to Mitchell Field as well as closer convenient parking lots to the
air terminal should entice more people to use Mitchell Field rather
than O'Hare.
The possibilities for alternate locations for the proposed Freeway-Airport connection are limited because the location of the terminal points are somewhat controlled. The east terminus is controlled by the proposed development of the terminal facilities of General Mitchell Field located just east of Howell Avenue. The terminus is fixed by an adequate interchange location to existing I-94.
